title: Select all (CTRL+A) not working on directories or desktop after mapping

status.label: Investigate the Explorer-only shortcut failure
status.detail: The author confirmed that Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A still fails on the desktop and in directories on the latest version, while working in other applications; screenshots confirm the mapping.

judgment.rationale: The initial report describes Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A on a Spanish Windows 11 system. In a follow-up, the author says the failure persists on the latest PowerToys version, supplies screenshots of the exact mapping and Keyboard Manager configuration, and gives numbered steps: the remap fails on directories or the desktop but works in Word, browsers, and other applications. This isolates an application-context difference and supports a focused investigation of how the remap reaches the Windows shell. The exact current build number is not stated.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.99.1, Windows 11, Spanish language, and PowerToys running as administrator.
The author says the mapping is Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A and that Ctrl+E is the native select-all shortcut in their Spanish environment.
The author confirms the failure still occurs on the latest version and supplies screenshots showing the Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A mapping.
The numbered follow-up says the mapping fails on a directory or desktop but works in applications such as Word and Chrome.
The issue has three comments and no assignees.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the app-versus-shell difference on the current build, then trace how Keyboard Manager's remapped Ctrl+A is delivered to Explorer and the desktop.

fix_assessment.rationale: The author confirms current behavior and shows the same mapping works in ordinary applications but not in Explorer or the desktop. This supports investigating a shell-specific remap delivery or shortcut interaction, though the underlying mechanism has not been identified.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A remapping in Windows shell surfaces
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Windows Explorer or the desktop may handle Ctrl+E/Ctrl+A differently from ordinary applications, preventing Keyboard Manager's replacement shortcut from reaching the shell's select-all command.
plan: Reproduce the exact Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A mapping on current stable in a directory, on the desktop, and in Word or a browser.
Trace Keyboard Manager's input and output events for the Explorer and desktop processes, comparing them with the working application case.

If the original Ctrl+E event or synthesized Ctrl+A is intercepted or suppressed in the shell path, adjust the remapping behavior so the shell receives the intended Ctrl+A without breaking its other Ctrl+E behavior.
Add regression coverage for the mapping in File Explorer, the desktop, and a standard application.
verification: Ctrl+E selects all items in a File Explorer directory and on the desktop when mapped to Ctrl+A.
The same mapping continues to work in standard applications.
Disabling Keyboard Manager restores the system's native Ctrl+E behavior, and unrelated Explorer shortcuts remain unaffected.

confidence.rationale: The current failure and app-versus-shell difference are confirmed with screenshots and numbered steps, but no event trace establishes whether Explorer intercepts the original key or does not receive the synthesized Ctrl+A.

issue_context.summary: Ctrl+E mapped to Ctrl+A still fails to select all on the desktop and in directories in the latest PowerToys version, while the mapping works in other applications.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.99.1, Windows 11, Spanish language, and PowerToys running as administrator.
The author says Ctrl+E is the native select-all shortcut and maps it to Ctrl+A.
The author says the behavior still occurs on the latest version and supplied screenshots showing the mapping.
The follow-up steps say the remap fails on a directory or desktop but works in Word, browsers, and other applications.
The exact current PowerToys build number is not provided.
inferences: The failure may be specific to the Windows shell's handling of the original or synthesized shortcut rather than a general remapping failure.
issue_context.analysis: The current confirmation and app-versus-shell comparison support a focused Keyboard Manager investigation. Reproduce in File Explorer and on the desktop, then inspect the delivered key sequence before choosing a code change; obtain the exact current build number to make the reproduction unambiguous.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and all three comments.
Inspected the two follow-up screenshots; the configuration shows Ctrl+E assigned to Ctrl+A.
Confirmed the author says the issue persists on the latest version and provided numbered reproduction steps.

information_gaps.information: The exact current PowerToys version/build used for the latest-version reproduction
information_gaps.why_needed: The issue confirms the bug is current but does not name the build, which is needed to reproduce and compare behavior consistently.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Read the PowerToys version from Settings > General and reply with the full version number used for the screenshots and retest.

actions.label: Approve the Windows shell remap investigation

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that Ctrl+E to Ctrl+A still fails on the desktop and in directories but works in other applications, and for sharing the mapping screenshots. Could you share the full PowerToys version number shown in Settings > General for the latest-version retest?
